# COUNTS: 19 write tools. 4 carry destructive. 8 apply IMMEDIATELY with no handshake.
#         6 audit under a name that is NOT the name the agent called.
## PART 4 — THE FIVE FINDINGS THAT SURVIVE, in descending commercial weight
# F1 🔴 THE `destructive` FLAG IS ON THE REVERSIBLE TOOL AND OFF THE IRREVERSIBLE ONE.
#   `reset_attempts` carries write:users and NOT destructive. With delete_module=True it
#   calls lms.djangoapps.instructor.enrollment.reset_student_attempts(delete_module=True),
#   which DELETES the learner's StudentModule row — their submitted state for that block —
#   and fires score-changed signals. There is no undo.
#   Meanwhile `deactivate_user` only flips is_active=False — request_retirement's OWN
#   docstring calls it "the reversible is_active flag" — and it DOES carry destructive.
#   🔵 CONSEQUENCE: a key provisioned ["read","write:users"] deliberately WITHOUT
#   destructive, so that it cannot delete, CAN delete a learner's submitted work, and
#   CANNOT deactivate an account. The guard is inverted on exactly the pair where it matters.
# F2 🔴 THE AUDIT LOG IS APPEND-ONLY IN ITS DOCSTRING AND DELETABLE IN ITS ADMIN.
#   models.py: "MCPAuditLog — append-only record of every state-changing tool call",
#   "Never updated after write." No save() or delete() override exists on the model.
#   admin.py MCPAuditLogAdmin overrides has_add_permission -> False,
#   has_change_permission -> False, and every field readonly — 🔴 but NOT
#   has_delete_permission, which Django defaults to user.has_perm("delete_mcpauditlog"),
#   and declares no `actions`, so it KEEPS the default "Delete selected objects" bulk action.
#   🔵 Add is blocked, change is blocked, DELETE is open — including in bulk, from the UI.
#   🔴 SECOND, INDEPENDENT PATH, needing no delete permission on the log at all:
#   MCPAuditLog.key and .user are both on_delete=models.SET_NULL. Deleting a key or a user
#   NULLs the attribution on every audit row it produced. The rows survive; the actor does not.
# F3 🔴 THE PII THE RETIREMENT TOOL REMOVES IS RETAINED BY THE RETIREMENT TOOL'S OWN AUDIT ROW.
#   _rails.redact() redacts {confirm_token, password, key, secret, token}. It does NOT
#   redact `username` or `email`. request_retirement's payload is {"username": ..., "full": ...},
#   so the audit row permanently stores the username of a learner whose account was retired
#   precisely to remove their PII. No retention or anonymisation hook ties the two together:
#   a grep of native/retirement.py and settings/ for retention|purge|anonymi|MCPAuditLog
#   returns nothing. 🔵 This is the GDPR erasure question a DPO asks, and the answer is in code.
# F4 🟡 SCOPE NARROWING DOES NOT APPLY TO SUPERUSERS OR TO JWT/SESSION CALLERS — BY DESIGN,
#   AND THE PACKAGE'S OWN TESTS ASSERT IT. require_scopes() returns early on
#   request.user.is_superuser; granted_scopes() returns ALL_SCOPES when there is no key.
#   tests/test_auth.py: test_superuser_bypasses_scope_narrowing,
#   test_jwt_or_session_request_has_all_scopes. 🟢 So this is INTENDED, not a bug.
#   🔴 But models.py sells scopes as "least privilege per credential", and for the superuser
#   who is most likely to mint an ops key, the scope list is decorative. And set_role can
#   grant `superuser` (behind grant:admin), which SILENTLY WIDENS every narrow key that user
#   already holds. State the limit when quoting the scope model to a client.
# F5 🔴 SIX OF NINETEEN WRITE TOOLS AUDIT UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME, AND TWO COLLAPSE INTO ONE.
#   create_block and create_block_tree BOTH audit as `create_xblock`. create_block_tree
#   creates an arbitrary-depth subtree in one call, applies to the draft immediately
#   (require_confirm=False), and shares create_block's 200-calls/60s budget.
#   🔵 So the audit trail cannot distinguish "created one block" from "created a course tree",
#   and an auditor joining an agent transcript to MCPAuditLog.tool on 6 of 19 write tools
#   joins on nothing. A compliance trail whose join key differs from the caller's is not a trail.
## PART 5 — what this does NOT establish
# 🔴 NO TOOL WAS CALLED. 33 registrations is what tools/list would show a client, not 33
#   verified mutations. Rails were read, not exercised.
# 🔴 The rate limiter FAILS OPEN by design (check_rate_limit catches Exception -> True), and
#   both the limiter and the confirm-token store use the ambient Django cache. guards.py says
#   so: under LocMemCache both are PER-PROCESS, so N workers give N x the stated budget.
#   Tutor ships memcached, so this is a configuration risk, not a defect of the package.
# 🔴 The facade has NO repository address. openedx-mcp 0.1.5 declares no project_urls and no
#   home_page on PyPI; every byte above came from the sdist. The artefact where ALL
#   authorisation lives is auditable only as a package payload. Bus factor stays 1.
# 🔴 Version skew: the plugin's README pins `openedx-mcp==0.1.4` as its example; 0.1.5 is
#   current. Everything above is 0.1.5.
